newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end higher on sentiment upturn.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end higher on sentiment upturn.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares rose 1.4 percent on Friday due to improved sentiment after rises in the previous two days, brokers said.
But volume remained relatively thin with many investors unwilling to return to buy in force because of uncertainty about the future direction of the market, they said.
The B share index rose 1.020 points or 1.36 percent to 75.861 points on volume of 10.513 million shares worth $6.376 million.

B shares began to stage a rebound on Wednesday after steady falls since July 1, when the former British colony of Hong Kong returned to Chinese rule. The Hong Kong handover had served as a major positive factor for the market.
"The B shares gained because previous falls were overdone," said a broker at Shenzhen J&A Securities in Shanghai. "But the expectations of investors are still not that good."
Investors took heart at the absence of negative news, but continued to tread cautiously due to worries that the government may yet take steps to stabilise the market, brokers said.
"With the approach of the interim results reporting season, investors are seeking companies whose results will improve," said another local broker.
Of 45 B shares, 41 traded with 23 up, 10 down and eight flat.
Brokers said smaller, second- and third-line stocks also attracted buying attention on Friday as their prices looked cheap following falls last week and early this week.
Shanghai Sanmao Textiles Co was the top B share gainer on bargain hunting, rising $0.012 or 9.09 percent to $0.144.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development Co was the most heavily traded B share. The stock was hit by profit taking, falling $0.012 or 0.94 percent to $1.268 on volume of 850,080 shares.
Domestic currency A shares rebounded on Friday from a minor fall the previous session on improved sentiment, brokers said.
The A index rose 36.733 points or 3.14 percent to 1,206.722 points on volume of 376.044 million shares worth 4.558 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index rose 101.394 points or 2.75 percent to to 3,793.472 points.
"If there is no negative news over the weekend, then the (A and B) markets should be stable on Monday," the J&A broker said.
With investors beginning to pick up shares of companies expected to post good interim results, the buying could help drag the overall market higher next week, brokers said.
Listed companies are required to announce their 1997 interim results by the end of August.
"Technically the market looks set to move up slightly in the short term," said the local broker.
